records.public_safe_text: on november 2, 2017, at approximately 1254 hours, [roadway], north of the raymond stotzer intersection, in reference to a vehicle versus pedestrian accident. information from dispatch was that a vehicle had struck a pedestrian, the pedestrian was complaining of arm pain, and college police and fire were on scene. upon arrival, at approximately 1258 hours, i observed a silver in color [roadway] just south of the crosswalk located across from the north entrance of parking area 36a. unit two (pedestrian), cesiah aparicio, identified by her tx id # 36287072 was in the back of the college station fire department ambulance. at approximately 1301 hours, [medical facility] by csfd for arm pain and cuts and scrapes from the roadway. unit one (driver), kacy petersen, identified by her tx dl # 35061740, advised that she [roadway] going the speed limit of 30 mph when she looked at the crosswalk and saw a big group of subjects. petersen advised she didn't see aparicio in the crosswalk and then she hit aparicio with her vehicle. petersen advised aparicio rolled over her vehicle and she then came to a stop in the roadway. petersen advised that aparicio was in the crosswalk when she hit aparicio. petersen advised once again she didn't see aparicio. unit one was identified by texas license plate of cx7w739 as a 2003 toyota camry being silver in color. at approximately 1324 hours, i spoke to a witness, marjorie nguyen, identified by her name and date of birth (dob [date]). nguyen advised she was traveling right behind unit one when she saw the bus was stopped [roadway], saw the flashing signal lights for the crosswalk as though they had been pushed. nguyen advised that unit one was already close to the crosswalk when she observed unit two crossing the roadway at the crosswalk. nguyen advised she saw unit one's brake lights came on but unit one could not stop and struck unit two. nguyen advised that after being struck unit two went up onto the hood, then the windshield, over the top of unit one and then came off of the back end of unit one to the ground.

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date], unit 1 was traveling wb on the 2600 block of e tom landry fwy at approximately 60mph [roadway] of traffic. unit 1 was proceeding wb with the flow of traffic when the driver of unit 1, brooks, raven, b/f, [date], observed unit 2 [roadway] of traffic with the hazard lights on. unit 1 attempted to brake to avoid collision, slid several feet while braking, and impacted the tail end of unit 2 causing front end distributed damage to unit 1 and minimal back distributed damage to unit 2. brooks did advise her left forearm was sore from the accident but declined medical attention. unit 2 had become disabled due to the hood opening while the vehicle was in operation, obstructing the operator's view. unit 2 then came to [roadway] of traffic, with the hazard lights turned on, for approximately 15 seconds according to the vehicle's operator, mckenzie, billy, b/m, [date]. both shoulder accesses were cut off by cement barriers due to construction in the area leaving no space out of the lanes of traffic for the vehicle to safely stop at. as he could not see due to the hood constricting his view, mckenzie had exited his vehicle in an attempt to close the hood of the vehicle. it was at this time unit 2 was impacted by unit 1. mckenzie advised he could hear a vehicle breaking and then felt the impact of his vehicle in to his person. the impact knocked him backward and on to the pavement. he did advise an injury to his knee, was treated by ems on scene, and refused transport by medical services for evaluation. after the impact, mckenzie had gotten up, checked on the driver of unit 1, and waited for officers to arrive. according to witnesses in the vehicle behind unit 2, mulholland, emma, w/f, [date] and duplanty, sarah, w/f, [date], unit 1 was traveling with the flow [roadway] of traffic. the witnesses observed the hazard lights of unit 2 and saw unit 1 attempt to brake to avoid collision. unit 1 could be heard by witnesses braking for several seconds in an attempt to avoid collision before impact between units 1 and 2. the witnesses then saw mckenzie come from in front of the pickup and approach the driver side of unit 1 in an effort to render aid. per sgt approval, no citations were issued at this time for the accident due to the construction area limiting the roadway and the heavy flow of traffic limiting evasive driving.

pedestrian. the wi-01 said she got the child and took her to near by (sierra) medical center for medical evaluation. wi-02 grandparent to the pedestrian stated he was working [roadway] from where the child was. the wi-02 said he heard the child calling out to him. the witness said he turned to see u1 hit the pedestrian [medical facility] where the officer was advised that per procedure all trauma patients [medical facility]. the child (pedestrian) was located at umc. medical staff advised that the child had not suffered any broken bones. the driver of u1 was not cited. wi-01 was cited due to the fact that the child was under her care and custody and she had noticed the child near the edge of the roadway and failed to act to prevent the child form encroaching on the roadway. wi-01 (aunt):
